STANZA I
Let every tongue thy goodness speak
Let every tongue thy goodness speak,
Thou sovereign Lord of all;
Thy strengthening hands uphold the weak,
And raise the poor that fall.
The psalm it sets
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 145:14, 17–21, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

14The LORD upholds all who fall and lifts up all who are bowed down. 17The LORD is righteous in all His ways and kind in all His deeds. 18The LORD is near to all who call on Him, to all who call out to Him in truth. 19He fulfills the desires of those who fear Him; He hears their cry and saves them. 20The LORD preserves all who love Him, but all the wicked He will destroy. 21My mouth will declare the praise of the LORD; let every creature bless His holy name forever and ever. PSALM 145:14, 17–21 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 145
When sorrow bows the spirit down, Or virtue lies distrest Beneath some proud oppressor's frown, Thou giv'st the mourners rest. STANZA II
